title: Al-Nur Workwear Overheating Incident in Dubai
premise: Two construction workers in Dubai suffered third-degree burns when a defective temperature sensor caused their electrically heated workwear to overheat during a cold-weather shift.

side_A.role: an advocate at a consumer-safety group
side_A.goal: pushing for a recall of the product

side_B.goal: showing the product is safe when used as directed

documents:
=== DOCUMENT 1: Incident Report and Site Log - Al-Mina Tower Construction Site ===

**Date:** November 12, 2023
**Incident ID:** AMT-2023-1112-04
**Location:** Zone 4, Al-Mina Tower, Dubai
**Reported By:** Site Safety Manager

**1. Incident Overview**
At 06:15 AM on November 12, 2023, workers Khalid Al-Farsi and Omar Hassan commenced their shift in Zone 4, an area designated for heavy equipment operation. The ambient temperature recorded at the site was 14 degrees Celsius. Both workers were issued Model X-900 heated jackets manufactured by Al-Nur Industrial Apparel, with serial numbers 889-A and 889-B respectively.

**2. Timeline of Events**
*   **06:15 AM:** Workers begin shift. Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) require immediate reporting of any temperature anomaly to the site supervisor.
*   **07:00 AM:** Discrepancy noted in communication logs regarding worker reporting. (See Section 4 for conflicting accounts).
*   **07:45 AM:** Temperature sensors in both jackets simultaneously registered a reading of 65 degrees Celsius. This reading exceeded the maximum safe operating surface temperature of 45 degrees Celsius specified in the X-900 user manual.
*   **07:45 AM - 09:15 AM:** Workers remained in Zone 4 for approximately 90 minutes after the initial shift start. They reported heat discomfort and subsequently removed their jackets.
*   **09:15 AM:** Medical team assessed workers. Third-degree burns were identified.

**3. Equipment and Product History**
The jackets in question were purchased by the construction company on October 1, 2023. The purchase falls within the standard 12-month warranty period provided by Al-Nur Industrial Apparel. The specific manufacturing batch for serial numbers 889-A and 889-B passed 100 percent of quality control tests during the manufacturing process. The jackets were stored in a temperature-controlled warehouse prior to distribution to the site.

**4. Reporting and Communication Discrepancies**
There is a conflict in the records regarding the workers' adherence to reporting protocols between 06:15 AM and 07:45 AM.
*   **Account A (Occupational Health Specialist):** States that workers attempted to report heat discomfort at 07:00 AM, but the supervisor did not respond due to a radio communication failure.
*   **Account B (Site Safety Manager):** States that no report was received until 07:45 AM, citing a violation of the SOP which mandates immediate reporting.

**5. Insurance and Liability**
Al-Nur Industrial Apparel’s liability insurance policy covers up to 1 million AED per incident. The construction company signed a Service Level Agreement (SLA) with Al-Nur ensuring a 24-hour response to equipment failures.

=== DOCUMENT 2: Medical Evaluation Report - Al-Dubai Medical Center ===

**Patient 1: Khalid Al-Farsi**
**Date of Evaluation:** November 12, 2023
**Attending Physician:** Dr. S. Rahman

**Clinical Findings:**
Patient presented with acute thermal injury. Examination reveals third-degree burns covering 12 percent of the torso. The burn pattern is consistent with contact with a heated garment.
**Medical History:** Review of patient records indicates no prior history of skin conditions or burn sensitivity.
**Incident Context:** Patient was wearing Model X-900 heated jacket (Serial No. 889-A) at the time of injury.

**Patient 2: Omar Hassan**
**Date of Evaluation:** November 12, 2023
**Attending Physician:** Dr. S. Rahman

**Clinical Findings:**
Patient presented with acute thermal injury. Examination reveals third-degree burns covering 10 percent of the arms. The burn pattern is consistent with contact with a heated garment.
**Medical History:** Review of patient records indicates no prior history of skin conditions or burn sensitivity.
**Incident Context:** Patient was wearing Model X-900 heated jacket (Serial No. 889-B) at the time of injury.

**Note:** Both patients were treated for shock and pain management. Referral to burn unit for ongoing care.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Email Correspondence - Al-Nur Industrial Apparel vs. Consumer Safety Alliance ===

**From:** Sarah Jenkins, Chief Engineer, Consumer Safety Alliance
**To:** Ahmed Al-Rashid, Head of Communications, Al-Nur Industrial Apparel
**Date:** November 13, 2023
**Subject:** Urgent: Technical Failure Analysis of X-900 Incident

Mr. Al-Rashid,

Following the incident at Al-Mina Tower on November 12, our engineering team has reviewed the preliminary data. We must address the technical nature of the failure immediately.

Your company claims that the sensors failed in a "closed-circuit" manner, which would theoretically turn off the heating elements, and that a separate relay fault kept the power on. This is a highly complex and unlikely scenario for a failure of this magnitude.

Our analysis suggests a different mechanism. The sensors failed in an **open-circuit**. This failure mode causes the heating elements to run continuously without any shutdown mechanism because the control board loses the signal to stop the heat. This is a fundamental design flaw in the safety architecture of the X-900. We urge you to provide the full diagnostic logs for serial numbers 889-A and 889-B to verify this.

Furthermore, we note that Al-Nur Industrial Apparel has issued 15 product recall notices in the last five years for other product lines. While these do not involve the X-900, they raise questions about the overall quality control culture within your organization. We expect a transparent response regarding the specific failure mode of the sensors in this incident.

Regards,

Sarah Jenkins
Chief Engineer
Consumer Safety Alliance

***

**From:** Ahmed Al-Rashid, Head of Communications, Al-Nur Industrial Apparel
**To:** Sarah Jenkins, Chief Engineer, Consumer Safety Alliance
**Date:** November 13, 2023
**Subject:** Re: Urgent: Technical Failure Analysis of X-900 Incident

Ms. Jenkins,

Thank you for your email. We are reviewing the incident with full seriousness.

Regarding your technical assessment, we respectfully disagree. Our internal engineering review indicates that the sensors failed in a **closed-circuit** configuration. In this state, the heating elements are designed to turn off. However, we have identified a separate relay fault that kept the power on despite the sensor shutdown. This is a rare, dual-failure scenario.

We stand by the integrity of our manufacturing process. The X-900 model passed 100 percent of quality control tests during the manufacturing batch that included the two jackets involved in this incident. The jackets were stored in a temperature-controlled warehouse prior to distribution, ensuring they were in optimal condition.

We are committed to the SLA we have with the construction company and will provide a detailed technical report within 24 hours.

Sincerely,

Ahmed Al-Rashid
Head of Communications
Al-Nur Industrial Apparel

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statements - Al-Mina Tower Incident ===

**Statement 1: Khalid Al-Farsi**
**Date:** November 14, 2023

I want to be clear about what happened. I used the jacket for the first time on the day of the incident. I had never worn it before. The moment I put it on, it started to overheat immediately. It felt like I was holding a hot iron against my chest. I tried to tell the supervisor, but nobody seemed to care. The heat was unbearable. I didn't know what to do, so I just kept working until I couldn't take it anymore. The jacket was clearly defective from the start. I am a new worker, and they gave me this gear without any proper testing. It was a disaster waiting to happen. I didn't see any warning signs, just pure heat. I am angry that they didn't check the equipment before giving it to me.

**Statement 2: Omar Hassan**
**Date:** November 14, 2023

I have been using this jacket for three previous shifts without any issues. It worked perfectly fine on the first two days. I am confused about why it failed on the third day. I did not use it on the day of the incident until my shift started at 06:15 AM. I felt a strange warmth, but I thought it was just the heating function working. I did not report it immediately because I was focused on the heavy equipment operation in Zone 4. By the time I realized it was too hot, it was already 07:45 AM. I tried to take it off, but it was stuck. I am frustrated that the jacket failed after working for so long. I did my part by following the protocol until I physically couldn't. I did not ignore the heat; I was just trying to finish my task. The failure was sudden and unexpected.

=== DOCUMENT 5: Maintenance and Quality Control Logs - Al-Nur Industrial Apparel ===

**Log Entry: October 15, 2023**
**Item:** Model X-900 Heated Jackets (Serial Nos. 889-A, 889-B)
**Action:** Routine Servicing and Testing
**Result:** Passed. All sensors and heating elements functional.
**Technician:** H. Al-Mansoor

**Note:** The maintenance logs for the specific jackets involved in the incident show that they were serviced and tested successfully on October 15, 2023. This is two weeks prior to the incident. The logs indicate no anomalies were detected during this servicing.

**Customer Service Log Summary (Last 12 Months)**
**Product Line:** X-900
**Total Complaints:** 500
**Issue Type:** Heating issues
**Resolution Status:** All 500 complaints were resolved without injury.
**Note:** These complaints involved minor temperature fluctuations or sensor errors that were corrected via software update or minor part replacement. No incidents of third-degree burns were recorded in this period.

**Quality Assurance Director's Note:**
Hassan Al-Mansoor, Quality Assurance Director, confirms that the maintenance logs are accurate and have not been altered. The logs show a consistent history of successful testing for the batch in question. There is no record of previous complaints about the specific sensor batch associated with serial numbers 889-A and 889-B. The system integrity is maintained through daily backups and access controls.
